name: English
title: PC monitor on your phone: CPU, GPU, RAM live | SysWatch
description: SysWatch shows your Windows PC's CPU, GPU, temperatures, memory and network live on your Android phone, with alerts. Free, no ads, no account.
ogAlt: SysWatch: monitor your PC from your phone

hero.lead: SysWatch is a PC monitor for your phone. A small Windows app reads your CPU and GPU load and temperature, memory, network, storage and battery. Your Android phone shows them live, like a system monitor you can carry around, and tells you when one crosses a limit you set.

see.h2: Your PC stats on your phone, as they move
see.lead: Cards for CPU, GPU, memory, network, storage, battery and uptime, each with its own history graph. SysWatch only shows real readings: if your PC does not report something, it is left out.

items.d: One calm panel, big numbers, one accent colour.
items.alt: SysWatch Overview on an Android phone: CPU load at 81% with its history graph, then GPU, memory, network and storage cards

items.d: Set a limit on any gauge and choose how often it may repeat.
items.alt: Alert editor in SysWatch: watch CPU load, tell me when it goes above 90%, do not repeat for 5 minutes

items.d: Accent, theme, density and the order of the cards.
items.alt: SysWatch settings with seven accent colours, light, dark and true black themes, and a switch for each Overview card

items.d: A gallery of 24 always-on faces, previewed with your own readings.
items.alt: Standby face gallery with previews of the art faces Horizon, Blocks, Bauhaus, Ink, Weave and Bloom

alerts.h2: Know when your PC runs hot
alerts.lead: Set a limit on any gauge. Your phone tells you when it is crossed, so you can watch CPU and GPU temperature on your phone without staring at it.
points: Rules read as sentences, such as “CPU load above 90%” or “Battery level below 20%”.
Each limit is drawn as a red line on its gauge, bar and graph.
Limits on load, memory, battery, network speed, storage and temperatures.
A quiet period per alert, from 1 minute to 1 hour, so one spike is one notification.
One-tap starter alerts, and export and import as a file.

look.lead: Pick an accent and a theme, then put the cards in your order. It stays one calm panel either way.

cells.d: Amber, cyan, green, violet, rose or mono, or matched to your wallpaper on Android 12 and newer.
Bridge, Gauges, Strip charts, Ledger and Focus.
Choose which cards show and in what order, roomy or compact.

look.alt: SysWatch Overview in landscape with the light theme: a wide CPU graph above GPU, memory and network cards
look.cap: A wide layout for landscape and tablets, in light or dark.

standby.h2: A second screen for your desk
standby.lead: Stand the phone next to your keyboard and it becomes a second screen for your PC stats: 24 always-on standby faces, 16 instruments and 8 art faces, in portrait and landscape.

faces.alt: Ink standby face: CPU load as a large serif 62% with GPU, memory, network and storage listed below
Bauhaus standby face: a red disc inside a blue ring, CPU at 10% and bars for GPU, memory and storage
Blocks standby face: red, cream, blue and yellow blocks sized by CPU, GPU, memory and storage

points: 8 art faces: Horizon, Blocks, Bauhaus, Ink, Weave, Bloom, Type and Pixel. Ink sets your readings like a printed page; Bauhaus turns CPU, GPU and memory into shapes.
16 instrument faces, picked from a gallery that previews each one with your own readings.
Burn-in protection, and an optional dim after 30 seconds.
A home screen widget in four looks: rings, bars, numerals, trace.

connect.lead: Both apps ask the same question the first time they open. Pick the same answer on each. You can change it later in Settings.

modes.name: Local
modes.note: Not encrypted on the local network, so use it on a network you trust.

modes.name: Cloud by DevLune
modes.note: Readings and your phone's name pass through the relay. You never enter any server details.

modes.name: Tailscale
vals: Through your own private Tailscale link
modes.note: Tailscale encrypts the link. It is a separate app with a free personal plan.

connect.foot: Not sure? Pick Local if the phone usually sits near the PC. Local and Tailscale need the latest version of both apps.

setup.lead: No account and nothing to type: the QR code carries everything the phone needs.
setup.howto: How to monitor your PC from your phone with SysWatch

steps.d: Download the Windows installer and run it. The installer is not code signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen shows a warning: choose More info, then Run anyway. SysWatch then sits in the system tray.
Get SysWatch on Google Play and open it.
Open Pairing on the PC and scan the QR code with the phone.

items.d: A 6-character pairing code is the only thing linking phone and PC.
The phone can see readings. It cannot control, change or run anything on your PC.
Local mode keeps readings on your own network. It is not encrypted there, so use a network you trust, or Tailscale, which encrypts the link.
Cloud by DevLune passes readings, and your phone's name, through DevLune's relay so the phone can reach the PC from anywhere.
Running program names are not sent unless you switch that on. The camera is used only to scan the pairing QR code.
No cookies, no trackers, and nothing loaded from other sites.

items.a: Yes. SysWatch is free on the phone and on the PC, with no ads and no account. If it earns a place on your desk, you can sponsor SysWatch on GitHub.

items.q: Does it work away from home?
items.a: Yes, in two of the three connection modes. Cloud by DevLune works from anywhere with internet and needs no setup. Tailscale is instant and private from anywhere, after about five minutes of setup. Local works on the same Wi-Fi.
No. A 6-character pairing code is the only thing linking phone and PC. You scan one QR code and there is nothing to type.

items.q: What can the phone do to my PC?
items.a: Nothing. SysWatch is read only: the phone can see readings, and it cannot control, change or run anything on your PC.
SysWatch runs on Windows today: Windows 10 and Windows 11, 64-bit. The phone app needs Android 7.0 or newer.

items.q: Why does Windows warn about the installer?
items.a: The installer is not code signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen shows “Windows protected your PC”. Choose More info, then Run anyway. The SysWatch download and setup guide shows every screen.

Yes, when your PC reports it. SysWatch shows CPU and GPU temperature next to load, and NVIDIA graphics cards are read directly. CPU temperature depends on what your PC reports, and SysWatch never shows a reading your PC does not send.
The Android app is in English, German, French, Spanish and Russian.

items.q: How do I add my language?
items.a: Community translations are welcome, and no programming is needed: it is one text file per language. In the translations folder of the SysWatch repository on GitHub, copy en.xml, translate it and open a pull request. A merged translation reaches the app by itself, with no app update.

That depends on the connection you pick. In Local mode readings never leave your network. Over Tailscale they travel through your own private, encrypted link. With Cloud by DevLune, readings and your phone's name pass through DevLune's relay. Running program names are not sent unless you switch that on.

translate.p: The Android app ships in English, German, French, Spanish and Russian. Community translations are welcome: add your language, or fix a line that reads wrong in yours. A merged translation reaches the app by itself, with no app update.
translate.cta: Open the translations folder on GitHub
